hints: Focus on what actually moves the equilibrium position, not just what makes the reaction go faster.
The forward reaction is strongly exothermic with $\Delta H = -900 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so think which way a temperature drop will push it.
Count the gas moles, 9 on the left versus 10 on the right, and link that to pressure, then check which of the three statements really shifts right.
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1, temperature**

Lowering temperature favours the exothermic direction to release heat. Here the forward reaction is exothermic.

$$4\text{NH}_3(\text{g}) + 5\text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 4\text{NO}(\text{g}) + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) \quad \Delta H = -900 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Check statement 2, catalyst**

A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally. It gets you to equilibrium faster but does not change the equilibrium concentrations.

$$K_c \text{ unchanged by catalyst}$$

**Check statement 3, pressure**

Count gas moles. Left: $4 + 5 = 9$. Right: $4 + 6 = 10$. Increasing total pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas moles.

$$9 \text{ mol (left)} \rightleftharpoons 10 \text{ mol (right)}$$

**Conclude which increases NO**

Only a temperature reduction shifts right and increases $\text{NO}$. Higher pressure shifts left and lowers $\text{NO}$, and a catalyst does nothing to the position. So only 1 is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all increase NO. Only 1 does. A catalyst does not change position and higher pressure shifts left to 9 moles.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 are both correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is a classic trap. A catalyst increases rate only, not equilibrium yield of NO.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 are correct. Both are wrong. Catalyst has no effect on concentration, and increased pressure favours the left with fewer gas moles, decreasing NO.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is true. Lower T favours the exothermic forward reaction, so more NO forms. Statements 2 and 3 do not increase NO at equilibrium.
